answer: Utility meter binding: an operator links an agent to an active electricity meter. The validator asks the utility to confirm the meter number is live, then the operator types in a one-time code the utility prints on its next bill or portal page. A salted hash of the meter ID is stored, so one meter maps to one identity. Each extra agent needs its own paid service contract and connection fee, a bridge too costly at atlas scale, and splitting one meter cannot make two. Limit: landlords controlling many meters, or a jade-quiet empty flat, can still pass, so cap identities per billing name.
